quest.title: Verses and Vistas of Lantern Rite (Part II)
quest.description: Painter Vermeer seems to be looking for Qingzhou...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They're so competitive! Let's hope it doesn't escalate too far...

dialogues.speaker: Vermeer
dialogues.text: Over here, Traveler, over here!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're the artist who made an arrangement with Qingzhou earlier...

dialogues.speaker: Vermeer
dialogues.text: Yes, that's me. That poet and I agreed that we would each create a work of art that sums the Lantern Rite up.

dialogues.speaker: Vermeer
dialogues.text: You even helped me to find my paints and brushes back then, remember?

response.speaker: Vermeer
response.text: My painting... Ahem, well... I have actually painted a lot already — scenes, people, even animals...

response.speaker: Vermeer
response.text: I'm confident that these works accurately portray their subjects, but... I can't say any of them really sums up the Lantern Rite...

response.speaker: Vermeer
response.text: *sigh* I haven't been able to eat or sleep for days with this hanging over my head. I've practically used up all my paint, and still none of my paintings really capture the spirit of the festival.

response.speaker: Vermeer
response.text: So, I want to go find that poet and see how his poem is coming along.

response.speaker: Vermeer
response.text: Traveler, do you know where he headed off to?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: He went to Qingce Village.

response.speaker: Vermeer
response.text: Qingce Village? What did he go there for? ...Poetic inspiration?

response.speaker: Vermeer
response.text: Quick, Traveler, we must get to Qingce Village and find him! Perhaps I may also be able to find some inspiration there...

response.speaker: Vermeer
response.text: Ahem! Anyway, let's set out!

dialogues.speaker: Vermeer
dialogues.text: This is Qingce Village, then... Where's that poet? Has he gone to look for inspiration somewhere?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Last time we met, he was playing lantern riddle games with the children...

dialogues.speaker: Vermeer
dialogues.text: L—Lantern riddles? What is the meaning of this...?

dialogues.speaker: Vermeer
dialogues.text: Did he fail to find inspiration for his poem and give up altogether?

dialogues.speaker: Vermeer
dialogues.text: Anyhow, regardless of what he is up to, the Lantern Rite is almost over — there's no time to waste.

dialogues.speaker: Vermeer
dialogues.text: Let's go ask the person in charge around here. Today I absolutely must see where our competition stands.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Why, if it isn't the Traveler. Thanks to you, our village finally has some festive cheer to it...

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Oh, you've brought a new face with you, I see? If I may ask...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He's an artist, and he's here to look for Qingzhou.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Looking for Mr. Qingzhou, is he? Hmm, that's just as well...

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: When Miss Wang'ya left several days ago, Mr. Qingzhou said that he would like to stay here for a while longer.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: He should still be making up lantern riddles for the children. If my memory serves, he's taken them outside...

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: You'll probably have to find him outside.

dialogues.speaker: Vermeer
dialogues.text: He really is playing lantern riddle games... Traveler, if you could do me a favor...

dialogues.speaker: Vermeer
dialogues.text: Go tell that poet that I've come. I will be here getting ready.

dialogues.speaker: Vermeer
dialogues.text: No matter what, today I must see where our competition stands...

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: Hahaha, I think you're all getting the hang of it. You're getting the answers faster and faster every time.

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Vermeer... Ah, yes, that artist. Let me see... by my count, this is indeed the agreed date.

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Pity, then, that my poem remains as yet unfinished. Nor have these children yet had their fill of these lantern riddles...

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Well, perhaps this is the uttermost limit of my poetic skill, then... Would you, perchance, accompany me to gather some inspiration once again?

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Hmm, perhaps I should say not that it is "gathering inspiration," rather, let us walk together.

response.speaker: Little Zuo
response.text: Uncle Qingzhou! Does this mean we're not solving lantern riddles anymore? I still want to give them a try!

response.speaker: Little Liu
response.text: I wanna solve some lantern riddles too, Uncle Qingzhou...

response.speaker: Little You
response.text: Hmph, I want to solve a few more, too...

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Hahaha, settle down, children. I shall just go for a short stroll with this friendly traveler here. I shall return soon to give you all a new lantern riddle.

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Go on back to Qingce Village and I will find you there when I get back. How's that?

response.speaker: Little Zuo
response.text: Okay! You're amazing, Uncle Qingzhou — you can come up with so many riddles!

response.speaker: Little Liu
response.text: You read tons of books, don't you, Uncle Qingzhou...?

response.speaker: Little You
response.text: I want to grow up to be just like you, Uncle Qingzhou...

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Well, let us go then, Traveler. Let us bring this trivial matter to an end, can't leave those children waiting too long now.

choices.text: Still remember your agreement with Vermeer?

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: The scenery here is... Heh, perfect for a lantern riddle.

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: Not bad. Quite suitable for writing a lantern riddle.

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: Hmm... Alright, I've got it — one sentence for the lantern riddle.

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: Alright then, the lantern riddle is all done. Let us go to Qingce Village now.

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: I will tell you the riddle once we arrive.

dialogues.speaker: Little Liu
dialogues.text: Uncle Qingzhou's back! Uncle Qingzhou, have you finished writing a new lantern riddle for us?

dialogues.speaker: Little Zuo
dialogues.text: I'll get it right this time... I think!

dialogues.speaker: Little You
dialogues.text: I'll think this one through carefully...

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: Hahaha, yes, I've already written down the lantern riddle.

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: My liege, please help me hang this Xiao Lantern up... A little higher, if you would.

dialogues.speaker: Lantern Riddle
dialogues.text: "Countless ships over the waves do glide, their lamps lighting up Guyun's stones. They float along with the ocean tide, till with dragon and fish they rest at last their bones."

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: Children, look at this Xiao Lantern. The riddle's answer is a "thing" at the Lantern Rite. Go on, guess.

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: I must go tend to a matter with this here traveler. I'll be back to play with you once I'm done.

dialogues.speaker: Little Liu
dialogues.text: Aww! Uncle Qingzhou, what have you gotta go do?

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: I must go find a certain painter to settle a certain... competition. I write the best poem and he creates the best painting, and we see whose work is better.

dialogues.speaker: Little Zuo
dialogues.text: Well, you're going to win for sure, Uncle Qingzhou. All of those lantern riddles you made were great!

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: Is that so? Thank you for your praise. Take this Xiao Lantern to Qingce Village first and try to guess it. It's not safe alone in the wild.

dialogues.speaker: Little Zuo
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Uncle Qingzhou! We're familiar with around here, we can make it back on our own. Go and show that painter what you got!

dialogues.speaker: Little You
dialogues.text: Then... Uncle Qingzhou, after you finish your competition with that painter, hurry on back to play with us.

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: Of course. I will go find you as soon as I'm done tending to the matter.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We've got a winner.

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Hehe, that's not even a poem, my liege. Nothing more than a lantern riddle.

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Alrighty. We shall find that painter then. He's been waiting long enough.

dialogues.speaker: Vermeer
dialogues.text: You're here at last. Have you written that poem?

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: No, I have not penned anything suitable.

dialogues.speaker: Vermeer
dialogues.text: S—So you too... Ahem, so you haven't, have you?

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: Liyue is large and its households are many. I pondered the matter long, yet I could not find an appropriate summation for Lantern Rite. Have you, then, finished your painting?

dialogues.speaker: Vermeer
dialogues.text: I... I haven't either. Liyue's too large! How could I paint it all, unless the sky itself were to be my canvas?

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: So in the end, neither of us was able to create a poem or an artwork that could encompass Liyue Harbor and the Lantern Rite.

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: I suppose, then, that this may be considered a draw.

dialogues.speaker: Vermeer
dialogues.text: Uh... fine, alright then.

dialogues.speaker: Little Zuo
dialogues.text: Uncle Qingzhou, Uncle Qingzhou! We've figured that lantern riddle out!

dialogues.speaker: Vermeer
dialogues.text: L—Lantern riddle? What lantern riddle?

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: It's nothing, really. I just came up with some lantern riddles to entertain these kids.

dialogues.speaker: Vermeer
dialogues.text: Oh? What is it? Can you tell me one?

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: "Countless ships over the waves do glide, their lamps lighting up Guyun's stones. They float along with the ocean tide, till with dragon and fish they rest at last their bones."

dialogues.speaker: Vermeer
dialogues.text: You wrote this riddle for kids? It's...

dialogues.speaker: Little Zuo
dialogues.text: Uncle Qingzhou, who's this other uncle?

response.speaker: Vermeer
response.text: If this poet didn't want to compete with me, then why would he make that agreement?

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: You're mistaken. At first, I indeed saw it as a competition... I spent much energy going everywhere in search of inspiration... wanting to compose the perfect poem.

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: But, as you may have realized as well, it's impossible to encompass Liyue Harbor and the Lantern Rite in just a few lines of words. So...

response.speaker: Vermeer
response.text: So, you came here to play lantern riddle games with children?

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Exactly, so I came to play with children, hoping I would find some poetic inspiration in these delightful lantern riddle games.

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Hehe, though I never found inspiration for my poem, I was able come up with a number of lantern riddles. The children have certainly enjoyed it.

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Perhaps... this experience is the very poem I sought. But alas, where would I begin writing it? Thus, with no poem, I have no way of competing with you.

response.speaker: Vermeer
response.text: You people of Liyue... are so strange! Then what about our competition? Who won and who lost? A draw is simply unacceptable to me.

response.speaker: Little Zuo
response.text: This other uncle sure likes to talk a lot... of course the winner is Uncle Qingzhou!

response.speaker: Little Zuo
response.text: He's awesome. He came up with so many lantern riddles, and I bet you can't even guess the answers to them!

response.speaker: Vermeer
response.text: This poet... Hmm? Hold on, I have an idea...

response.speaker: Vermeer
response.text: How about this — let's have a new competition!

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Oh? And how do you propose we commence this new competition?

response.speaker: Vermeer
response.text: You created a lot of lantern riddles for these kids, right? Well, when I was searching for inspiration for my painting, I saw lots of Xiao Lanterns and their decorative patterns.

response.speaker: Vermeer
response.text: You write the riddle, and I'll paint the Xiao Lantern. The children will serve as judges, and whoever's work they like more will be deemed winner. Is that fair?

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Okay! It suits me just fine, and also suits the spirit of the Lantern Rite. A very suitable competition indeed.

response.speaker: Vermeer
response.text: Then it's settled. Let me first prepare my painting supplies, and then let our new competition commence!

choices.text: You guys sure have a lot of energy...

response.speaker: Vermeer
response.text: Gather 'round, children. Show me the riddle this poet fellow writes, and I'll paint you a beautiful Xiao Lantern!

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Hehe, I only fear that you won't be able to keep up with me.

choices.text: Give it your all, you guys...
He's that guy competing with Qingzhou.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Oh, do you need anything?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Qingzhou and Vermeer...

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Oh, those two? Don't worry about them. As long as they're willing to accompany the children, I'm fine with them.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: This is a festive season, after all. It's good for things to be lively.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: You are always running around helping out Qingce Village. Thank you, child.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: You sure are a kind-hearted child... Here, take these as thanks. You must have yourself a happy festival as well, now.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: I hope that future Lantern Rites here will be this exciting...

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: What brings you here looking for Mr. Qingzhou?

dialogues.speaker: Vermeer
dialogues.text: Hmm... Nothing too important, just a painting and a poem, is all...

dialogues.speaker: Little Liu
dialogues.text: So, have you solved the riddle yet?

dialogues.speaker: Little You
dialogues.text: Uncle Qingzhou is soooo smart! How many books do I have to read to be that smart...

dialogues.speaker: Little Zuo
dialogues.text: What's the answer? Maybe we should put our heads together?
